title: Live updates: Bitcoin slips back under $60,000 as HYPE leads altcoins lower
content: HYPE fell 8% and SOL 5%, and one analyst said a recovery will need selling in stocks to ease first, with U.S. inflation data due before Thanksgiving.

title: Solana developers move to stop validators finishing work on blocks that already lost
content: The fix would stop the computers that run Solana from wasting effort on transactions the network has already thrown out, freeing up power its recent speed upgrade didn't touch.

title: Just 10 accounts drove all of the XRP Ledger's trading growth last quarter
content: Data shows that the ten busiest accounts accounted for more than all of the exchange's quarterly growth, while trading by everyone else declined.

title: Crypto traders can now hedge Nvidia, Anthropic and oil bets on Derive
content: Derive’s new options on Nvidia, Anthropic, stock indices and oil bring hedging tools to onchain RWA markets.

title: A year after buying bitcoin, Czech central bank won't say what it's worth
content: The Czech National Bank bought bitcoin a year ago as an experiment. The coin has fallen at least 40% since, and the bank's audited accounts carry it at cost rather than market value. The CNB told CoinDesk an outside custodian holds the coins.

title: EU seeks up to $55B for AI and quantum computing fund: Report
content: Hackers already use AI to target crypto exchanges, while future quantum computers could break the cryptography that protects users’ funds.

title: South Korea’s crypto bill could move stablecoin race beyond token issuance
content: South Korea’s draft bill favors bank-led stablecoin issuance but allows fintech and technology companies to become the largest individual shareholders.

title: Solana DEX Velocity halts trading over bug just months after relaunch
content: Velocity relaunched in September as a rebuilt version of Drift Protocol, which was attacked by North Korean hackers in April.

title: Trump willing to pardon Jensen Huang, says it won’t be necessary
content: The president’s remarks come days before Jensen Huang is due to face congressional questioning over national security concerns and US chip export controls.

title: OpenAI and Anthropic Insiders Fear Their Next AI Models Are Too Dangerous to Release
content: Employees at both AI labs reportedly question whether their strongest models should ever reach the public, as researchers struggle to keep increasingly capable systems under control during training and testing.

title: Anthropic’s Claude Ship Lets AI Write, Review and Approve Its Own Code
content: Anthropic’s new coding tools can review and repair software changes before approving them for release, leaving development teams to decide when a human still needs to check the AI’s work.

title: Coldcard Bitcoin Exploit, Revisited: How a Hidden Flaw Survived Years of Audits
content: Coinkite’s postmortem reveals a software random-number generator shipped in place of the hardware one for over five years, slipping past at least 15 reviews.

title: Ethereum Foundation Says AI Is a More Urgent Threat Than Quantum Computing
content: The Ethereum Foundation has doubled its protocol security team and is prioritizing a cryptographic overhaul as advances in AI threaten the mathematical assumptions that keep billions in crypto safe.

title: Bitcoin Losses Are the Worst Since FTX. Is the Bottom Near?
content: Bitcoin slipped below $60,000 as realized losses nearly doubled in a week. Glassnode says the sell-off resembles past market bottoms, but another drop to $53,200 could be in the cards.
